Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: This ultimately led to the establishment of the _____ in Ifriqiya under the Imam–caliph Abdullah al-Mahdi Billah
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: This ultimately led to the establishment of the Fatimid Caliphate in Ifriqiya under the Imam–caliph Abdullah al-Mahdi Billah.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: However, Abdullah al-_____ quickly fell out with Abu Abdallah and had Abu Abdallah executed on 18 February 911
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: This ultimately led to the establishment of the Fatimid Caliphate in Ifriqiya under the Imam–caliph Abdullah al-Mahdi Billah. However, Abdullah al-Mahdi Billah quickly fell out with Abu Abdallah and had Abu Abdallah executed on 18 February 911.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Abu Abdallah joined the Hajj caravan to Mecca, and joined the _____ pilgrims on their return to their homeland
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Abu Abdallah joined the Hajj caravan to Mecca, and joined the Yemeni pilgrims on their return to their homeland.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: He arrived there in April 892, and stayed and learned with the chief Isma'ili da'i, in Yemen, _____, in preparation for going on to lead a mission to the Maghreb
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: He arrived there in April 892, and stayed and learned with the chief Isma'ili da'i, in Yemen, Ibn Hawshab, in preparation for going on to lead a mission to the Maghreb. After less than a year, Ibn Hawshab sent Abu Abdallah again to Mecca, thence to go on to the Maghreb.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: After less than a year, _____ sent Abu Abdallah again to Mecca, thence to go on to the Maghreb

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Following usual practice, he was to be accompanied by another da'i, Abdallah ibn Abi'l-_____, but the latter was replaced by Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Zabidi
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Following usual practice, he was to be accompanied by another da'i, Abdallah ibn Abi'l-Malahif, but the latter was replaced by Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Zabidi.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Ibrahim became Abu Abdallah's lieutenant, becoming known as "the lesser lord" (al-sayyid al-saghir) among Abu Abdallah's followers, and remained with him until the conquest of _____ in 909
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Ibrahim became Abu Abdallah's lieutenant, becoming called "the lesser lord" (al-sayyid al-saghir) among Abu Abdallah's followers, and remained with him until the conquest of Ifriqiya in 909. According to later sources, after engaging them in discussion, he found out about the situation in their homeland, the feebleness of the Aghlabid government outside the core territories of Ifriqiya, and the Berbers' own military potential.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: At Mecca, Abu Abdallah came across a party of _____ who were on the Hajj, to whom he presented himself as a native of Sana'a
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: At Mecca, Abu Abdallah came across a party of Kutama Berbers who were on the Hajj, to whom he presented himself as a native of Sana'a.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: His brother, Abu'l-Abbas, remained in Egypt and provided the link to the headquarters of the da'wa in _____
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: His brother, Abu'l-Abbas, remained in Egypt and provided the link to the headquarters of the da'wa in Salamiya.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Abu Abdallah secured the protection of the _____ clan and immediately began his missionary work, establishing a base in the scarcely populated area of Ikjan
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Abu Abdallah secured the protection of the Saktan clan and immediately began his missionary work, establishing a base in the scarcely populated area of Ikjan.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: The da'i made some powerful converts in the chieftains Abu Musa ibn Yunus al-Azayi, leader of the Masalta clan, and Abu Zaki Tammam ibn Mu'arik, nephew of the leader of the Ijjana.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: As a result, he soon had to move his base of operations from Ikjan to _____
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: As a result, he soon had to move his base of operations from Ikjan to Tazrut. Abu Abdallah modelled his activities on the example of Muhammad: Ikjan and Tazrut became an 'abode of refuge' (dar al-hijra), his followers were termed the 'friends' (awliya) or 'faithful' (mu'minun), a chosen people.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: This complacency came to an end in late 902, Abu Abdallah attacked and captured the fortified town of _____
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: This complacency came to an end in late 902, Abu Abdallah attacked and captured the fortified town of Mila. The capture of Mila forced the Aghlabids to react, sending an army west to recover the city, under the prince Abu Abdallah al-Ahwal, a son of Emir Abdallah II.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: The capture of Mila forced the Aghlabids to react, sending an army west to recover the city, under the prince Abu Abdallah al-Ahwal, a son of _____
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: The capture of Mila forced the Aghlabids to react, sending an army west to recover the city, under the prince Abu Abdallah al-Ahwal, a son of Emir Abdallah II. The expedition was further condemned to failure as the result of Aghlabid dynastic disputes: in July 903, Emir Abdallah II was murd.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: In 904, Abu Abdallah captured another major town, _____
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: In 904, Abu Abdallah captured another major town, Setif.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Emir Ziyadat Allah III obtained a juridical opinion lambasting the followers of "the man from Sana'a" as heretics, but his military response proved as ineffective as the last.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: An army under the prince Ibrahim al-Habashi was sent west but wintered at Constantine, before being joined by the forces of Shabib ibn Abi Shaddad, governor of the frontier province of Zab. Ibrahim al-Habashi led the combined Aghlabid army into the mountains in pursuit of the Kutama, but at Kayuna it was put to battle and destroyed by Abu Abdallah's men.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Ibrahim al-Habashi led the combined Aghlabid army into the mountains in pursuit of the Kutama, but at Kayuna it was put to battle and destroyed by Abu Abdallah's men.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: The Aghlabid government immediately raised another army and stationed it at al-Urbus (_____), barring the way to Kairouan and Raqqada
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: The Aghlabid government immediately raised another army and stationed it at al-Urbus (Byzantine Laribus), barring the way to Kairouan and Raqqada.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Tubna was placed under siege for almost a year, before it capitulated on terms in _____ 906: the garrison was spared, but the renegade Kutama chieftain Fath ibn Yahya al-Masaliti was executed
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Tubna was placed under siege for almost a year, before it capitulated on terms in October 906: the garrison was spared, but the renegade Kutama chieftain Fath ibn Yahya al-Masaliti was executed.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: The triumph of the da'i was helped by the uprising of the _____ army under Mudlij ibn Zakariyya in March 906
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: The Aghlabid government immediately raised another army and stationed it at al-Urbus (Byzantine Laribus), barring the way to Kairouan and Raqqada. As the historian Michael Brett comments, "this was an army on the defensive"; as a result, Abu Abdallah ignored it, and moved instead against Tubna (ancient Tubunae), seat of Shabib ibn Abi Shaddad, administrative and military centre of the Aghlabid frontier, and last refuge of the renegade Kutama chieftains.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: This military mutiny clearly showed that the _____ state was disintegrating, and Abu Abdallah pressed his advantage
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: As the historian Michael Brett comments, "this was an army on the defensive"; as a result, Abu Abdallah ignored it, and moved instead against Tubna (ancient Tubunae), seat of Shabib ibn Abi Shaddad, administrative and military centre of the Aghlabid frontier, and last refuge of the renegade Kutama chieftains. The triumph of the da'i was helped by the uprising of the Aghlabid army under Mudlij ibn Zakariyya in March 906.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Abu Abdallah spent 908 further south, at Kasserine and the Djerid, but in March 909 gathered his forces for the final assault.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: On 18 March 909, the _____ army was overwhelmed, and the inhabitants of al-Urbus massacred

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Abu Abdallah sent a thousand horse under one of his commanders ahead to put an end to the looting, and followed towards _____
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Abu Abdallah sent a thousand horse under one of his commanders ahead to put an end to the looting, and followed towards Kairouan.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: On the next day, 25 March 909, Abu Abdallah entered Raqqada and took up residence in the palace of the emir.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: With a small entourage he made his way to Ramla and thence Egypt, where they were sheltered by Abu Abdallah's old mentor, _____, for a year in 904–905
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: With a small entourage he made his way to Ramla and thence Egypt, where they were sheltered by Abu Abdallah's old mentor, Abu Ali, for a year in 904–905.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: In view of Abu Abdallah's successes, al-Mahdi decided to next move west towards Ifriqiya, and joined a merchant caravan going west, accompanied by Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: On the way, the caravan was attacked by Berber tribes, which left Abu'l-_____ wounded
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: In view of Abu Abdallah's successes, al-Mahdi decided to next move west towards Ifriqiya, and joined a merchant caravan going west, accompanied by Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad. On the way, the caravan was attacked by Berber tribes, which left Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad wounded.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: In view of Abu Abdallah's successes, al-Mahdi decided to next move west towards Ifriqiya, and joined a merchant caravan going west, accompanied by Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad. On the way, the caravan was attacked by Berber tribes, which left Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad wounded.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Unbeknownst to him, news of al-Mahdi and his identity as one sought by the Abbasid government had already reached the city, and he was immediately arrested.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: He remained in prison until spring of 906, when he was able to escape and left for _____
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: At Tripoli, Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad was sent ahead to Kairouan, the Aghlabid capital, to reconnoitre. He remained in prison until spring of 906, when he was able to escape and left for Tripoli.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Pressuring and even bribing the caravan leader to make haste, in late 905 they arrived in _____, an oasis town in eastern Morocco, ruled by the Midrarid dynasty and a centre of the trans-Sahara trade
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Pressuring and even bribing the caravan leader to make haste, in late 905 they arrived in Sijilmasa, an oasis town in eastern Morocco, ruled by the Midrarid dynasty and a centre of the trans-Sahara trade. With his master was still in faraway Sijilmasa, it was up to Abu Abdallah to establish the new Shi'a regime in Ifriqiya.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

With his master was still in faraway Sijilmasa, it was up to Abu Abdallah to establish the new Shi'a regime in Ifriqiya.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: On 26 _____ 909, the Kutama army reached Sijilmasa, and demanded the release of their captive imam
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: On 26 August 909, the Kutama army reached Sijilmasa, and demanded the release of their captive imam. On the next day, 27 August, al-Mahdi was enthroned and acclaimed by the troops.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: On 26 August 909, the Kutama army reached Sijilmasa, and demanded the release of their captive imam. On the next day, 27 August, al-Mahdi was enthroned and acclaimed by the troops.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages

Mounted on horseback and dressed in fine clothes, al-Mahdi and al-Qa'im were presented to the army, amidst shouts and tears of religious exaltation.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: An immediate conflict was averted as Abu Abdallah was called to lead an army east in July 910.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: The latter was quickly subdued by loyalist _____, and Abu Abdallah managed to defeat the Zenata near Tubna, relieving Tahert and even reaching the Mediterranean coast at Ténès

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.fact: Abu Abdallah, his brother Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad, Abu Zaki, and the 'supreme shaykh' Abu Musa Harun openly accused him of being a fraud and an impostor.

Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i.question: Informed of their intentions by the Kutama commander _____, al-Mahdi moved first

Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: Several other statesmen and military officers such as Ali Daya shortly joined Mas'ud, thus increasing his strength on his march to Ghazni.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: During this period, in the words of the historian _____, "Zawzani became a sort of vizier and rose in prestige and influence
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: During this period, in the words of the historian Yusofi, "Zawzani became a sort of vizier and rose in prestige and influence.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Mas'ud I shortly marched towards the Ghazni, where he successfully defeated _____ and imprisoned the latter
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: Mas'ud I shortly marched towards the Ghazni, where he successfully defeated Mohammad and imprisoned the latter. He then had Hasanak, who had supported Mohammad, imprisoned in Balkh.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: He then had _____, who had supported Mohammad, imprisoned in Balkh
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: He then had Hasanak, who had supported Mohammad, imprisoned in Balkh. Through the efforts of Zawzani, Mas'ud had Hasanak charged of infidelity, and had him executed.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Through the efforts of Zawzani, Mas'ud had _____ charged of infidelity, and had him executed
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: He then had Hasanak, who had supported Mohammad, imprisoned in Balkh. Through the efforts of Zawzani, Mas'ud had Hasanak charged of infidelity, and had him executed.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Meanwhile, Zawzani helped _____, who had been released from prison, to regain the vizier office
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: Meanwhile, Zawzani helped Ahmad Maymandi, who had been released from prison, to regain the vizier office.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Although Ahmad did not trust Zawzani, he appointed Zawzani as the chief administrator of the _____ army
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: Although Ahmad did not trust Zawzani, he appointed Zawzani as the chief administrator of the Ghaznavid army.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Despite the opposition of Ahmad, Zawzani managed to make Mas'ud regain riches from several officers which _____ had given to them in order to gain support
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: Despite the opposition of Ahmad, Zawzani managed to make Mas'ud regain riches from several officers which Mohammad had given to them in order to gain support.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: In _____, Zawzani managed to urge Mas'ud to assassinate the Ghaznavid governor of Khwarazm, Altun Tash, whom Zawzani suspected of treachery
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: In 1032, Zawzani managed to urge Mas'ud to assassinate the Ghaznavid governor of Khwarazm, Altun Tash, whom Zawzani suspected of treachery.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: However, _____ managed to survive the assassination and have the assassin captured
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: In 1032, Zawzani managed to urge Mas'ud to assassinate the Ghaznavid governor of Khwarazm, Altun Tash, whom Zawzani suspected of treachery. However, Altun Tash managed to survive the assassination and have the assassin captured.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Mas'ud, who feared that _____ would declare independence after the failed assassination attempt, had Zawzani imprisoned at Marw in order to avoid a rebellion
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: In 1032, Zawzani managed to urge Mas'ud to assassinate the Ghaznavid governor of Khwarazm, Altun Tash, whom Zawzani suspected of treachery. However, Altun Tash managed to survive the assassination and have the assassin captured.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: He also took Zawzani's wealth and servants, which had spread in many places such as Marw, _____, Ghur, Badghis, Ghazni, and Balkh
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: He also took Zawzani's wealth and servants, which had spread in many places such as Marw, Nishapur, Ghur, Badghis, Ghazni, and Balkh.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: In _____, Zawzani succeeded the deceased Abu Nasr Mushkan as the chief secretary
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: In 1040, Zawzani succeeded the deceased Abu Nasr Mushkan as the chief secretary. In 1040, Zawzani was present at the disastrous Battle of Dandanaqan against the Seljuq Turks, who managed to emerge victorious during the battle.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: In _____, Zawzani was present at the disastrous Battle of Dandanaqan against the Seljuq Turks, who managed to emerge victorious during the battle
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: In 1040, Zawzani succeeded the deceased Abu Nasr Mushkan as the chief secretary. In 1040, Zawzani was present at the disastrous Battle of Dandanaqan against the Seljuq Turks, who managed to emerge victorious during the battle.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: During this period, Zawzani had good relations with the historian Abul-_____, and helped him in some of his problems
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: During this period, Zawzani had good relations with the historian Abul-Fazl Bayhaqi, and helped him in some of his problems.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Because of this, _____ also helped Zawzani in his secretarial tasks
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: During this period, Zawzani had good relations with the historian Abul-Fazl Bayhaqi, and helped him in some of his problems. Because of this, Bayhaqi also helped Zawzani in his secretarial tasks.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: During the same period, a rebellion occurred under Abu'l-_____, which Zawzani was blamed for by Mas'ud, and was dismissed from his office, and sent to Bust
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: During the same period, a rebellion occurred under Abu'l-Fadl Kurnaki, which Zawzani was blamed for by Mas'ud, and was dismissed from his office, and sent to Bust.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: However, the army of Mas'ud shortly revolted against him, and had his brother _____ restored to the Ghaznavid throne
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: However, the army of Mas'ud shortly revolted against him, and had his brother Mohammad restored to the Ghaznavid throne. Mohammad then had Mas'ud imprisoned at Giri, where he was shortly executed either on the orders of Mohammad or Mohammad's son Ahmad.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Mohammad then had Mas'ud imprisoned at _____, where he was shortly executed either on the orders of Mohammad or Mohammad's son Ahmad
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: Mohammad then had Mas'ud imprisoned at Giri, where he was shortly executed either on the orders of Mohammad or Mohammad's son Ahmad.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: He then crowned himself as the new ruler of the _____, and restored Zawzani to the chief secretary office
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: He then crowned himself as the new ruler of the Ghaznavid Empire, and restored Zawzani to the chief secretary office.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: After this, Zawzani is much less mentioned in sources, but is known to have been living during the reign of _____'ud II, Ali, Abd al-Rashid, Toghrul, and Farrukh-Zad
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: After this, Zawzani is much less mentioned in sources, but is known to have been living during the reign of Sultan Mas'ud II, Ali, Abd al-Rashid, Toghrul, and Farrukh-Zad.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: Zawzani later died in _____
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: Zawzani later died in 1054.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: In 1040, Zawzani succeeded the deceased _____ as the chief secretary
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: In 1040, Zawzani succeeded the deceased Abu Nasr Mushkan as the chief secretary.

Abu Sahl Zawzani.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Sahl Zawzani.question: In 1040, Zawzani was present at the disastrous Battle of Dandanaqan against the _____, who managed to emerge victorious during the battle
Abu Sahl Zawzani.fact: In 1040, Zawzani was present at the disastrous Battle of Dandanaqan against the Seljuq Turks, who managed to emerge victorious during the battle.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: The _____ was Emir of Mosul from 967 to 978.
Abu Taghlib.fact: Uddat al-Dawla Abu Taghlib Fadl Allah al-Ghadanfar al-Hamdani (Arabic: عدة الدولة أبو تغلب فضل الله الغضنفر الحمداني, romanized: ʿUddat al-Dawla ʿAbū Taghlib Faḍl Allāh al-Ghaḍanfar al-Ḥamdanī), usually known simply by his kunya as Abu Taghlib, was the third Hamdanid ruler of the Emirate of Mosul, encompassing most of the Jazira. In 978, the Jazira was occupied by the Buyids of Shiraz under Bakhtiyar's cousin Adud al-Dawla, and Abu Taghlib fled to the Fatimid-controlled parts of Syria.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: There he tried to secure the governorship of _____, and became involved in local rivalries which resulted in his defeat in battle and execution on 29 August 979
Abu Taghlib.fact: There he tried to secure the governorship of Damascus, and became involved in local rivalries which resulted in his defeat in battle and execution on 29 August 979.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: His mother was a _____ woman, Fatima bint Ahmad, who reportedly exercised considerable influence over Nasir al-Dawla's affairs
Abu Taghlib.fact: His mother was a Kurdish woman, Fatima bint Ahmad, who reportedly exercised considerable influence over Nasir al-Dawla's affairs.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: Nasir al-Dawla had established the _____ as masters of a practically independent emirate encompassing the Jazira and centred on Mosul
Abu Taghlib.fact: Nasir al-Dawla had set up the Hamdanids as masters of a practically independent emirate encompassing the Jazira and centred on Mosul.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: The army of the _____'izz al-Dawla occupied Mosul and Nasir al-Dawla was once again forced to flee to the hill country of the northern Jazira
Abu Taghlib.fact: The army of the Buyid Mu'izz al-Dawla occupied Mosul and Nasir al-Dawla was once again forced to flee to the hill country of the northern Jazira.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: By 971 he had extended his control over all of _____ and Diyar Mudar, once part of Sayf al-Dawla's domain, uniting the entire Jazira under his rule
Abu Taghlib.fact: By 971 he had extended his control over all of Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar, once part of Sayf al-Dawla's domain, uniting the entire Jazira under his rule.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: Sa'd al-_____, deprived of his own capital and lacking any power to offer any resistance, tacitly accepted these losses as well as his cousin's suzerainty
Abu Taghlib.fact: Abu Taghlib seized not only the towns held by his brother, but also used the conditions of near-anarchy prevailing in Syria at the time and after Sayf al-Dawla's death to expand his territory at the expense of his cousin, Sa'd al-Dawla. By 971 he had extended his control over all of Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar, once part of Sayf al-Dawla's domain, uniting the entire Jazira under his rule.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: In 973, _____ finally persuaded Bakhtiyar to march north
Abu Taghlib.fact: As ruler of the Jazira, Abu Taghlib was one of the richest rulers of the region; Ibn Hawkal's descriptions attest to the wealth derived from the many Hamdanid estates, and Ibn Miskawayh, who was tasked with inventorying the family's mountain strongholds after the Buyid dissolution of the Hamdanid emirate in 979, writes of the immense cash reserves stored there. In 973, Hamdan finally persuaded Bakhtiyar to march north.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: Negotiations resulted in an agreement, but _____ regarded it as too favourable to the Hamdanid emir, and once more marched against Mosul
Abu Taghlib.fact: In 973, Hamdan finally persuaded Bakhtiyar to march north. Negotiations resulted in an agreement, but Bakhtiyar regarded it as too favourable to the Hamdanid emir, and once more marched against Mosul.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: The devastating raid was partly avenged through the defeat and capture of the Domestic of the _____ at Amid in 973, but in 974 Tzimiskes himself raided the Jazira in retaliation
Abu Taghlib.fact: The devastating raid was partly avenged through the defeat and capture of the Domestic of the Schools Melias at Amid in 973, but in 974 Tzimiskes himself raided the Jazira in retaliation.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: Once again, _____ persuaded him to march on Mosul, and Bakhtiyar led his forces to Tikrit
Abu Taghlib.fact: In 976, following the death of Tzimiskes, Abu Taghlib agreed to support the bid for the Byzantine throne of the rebel general Bardas Skleros, with whom he concluded a treaty whereby the Hamdanid ruler supplied Skleros with light cavalry in exchange for an unspecified marriage agreement. Once again, Hamdan persuaded him to march on Mosul, and Bakhtiyar led his forces to Tikrit.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: Bakhtiyar himself was captured and executed at the orders of his cousin, who then advanced on _____
Abu Taghlib.fact: Bakhtiyar himself was captured and executed at the orders of his cousin, who then advanced on Mosul. Adud al-Dawla took Mosul in June 978.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: Adud al-_____ took Mosul in June 978
Abu Taghlib.fact: In May 978, Bakhtiyar and Abu Taghlib were defeated in a battle near Samarra by Adud al-Dawla. Unlike earlier Buyid expeditions against the Hamdanids, that had failed chiefly because they were unable to sustain themselves in the Jazira, this was far better organized, as Adud al-Dawla brought along experienced administrators familiar with the area.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: He defeated a Buyid force pursuing him at Skleros' base of Kharput/_____ in August, but Skleros too was hard-pressed by the loyalist general Bardas Phokas to assist him
Abu Taghlib.fact: He defeated a Buyid force pursuing him at Skleros' base of Kharput/Hisn Ziyad in August, but Skleros too was hard-pressed by the loyalist general Bardas Phokas to assist him.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: His renewed offers for a negotiated settlement were rebuffed by Adud al-Dawla, as the Buyid ruler completed his conquest of the _____
Abu Taghlib.fact: His renewed offers for a negotiated settlement were rebuffed by Adud al-Dawla, as the Buyid ruler completed his conquest of the Jazira. With Buyid control over most of the Jazira solidified, Skleros's revolt ending in defeat in March 979, and unable to seek aid from his cousin Sa'd al-Dawla, who had already acknowledged Adud al-Dawla's suzerainty and was under orders to arrest him, Abu Taghlib with his remaining followers crossed the Syrian Desert to the Fatimid-controlled south of Syria.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: There he became embroiled in the complex power struggles between the _____ government and local elites
Abu Taghlib.fact: With Buyid control over most of the Jazira solidified, Skleros's revolt ending in defeat in March 979, and unable to seek aid from his cousin Sa'd al-Dawla, who had already acknowledged Adud al-Dawla's suzerainty and was under orders to arrest him, Abu Taghlib with his remaining followers crossed the Syrian Desert to the Fatimid-controlled south of Syria. There he became embroiled in the complex power struggles between the Fatimid government and local elites.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: It was in this context that Abu Taghlib is first mentioned in _____, when his father had once again been embroiled in a conflict with the Buyids
Abu Taghlib.fact: It was in this context that Abu Taghlib is first mentioned in 964, when his father had once again been embroiled in a conflict with the Buyids.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: He endeavoured to gain recognition by the _____ as governor of Damascus, but the rebel general al-Qassam, who held the city, repulsed him
Abu Taghlib.fact: He endeavoured to gain recognition by the Fatimids as governor of Damascus, but the rebel general al-Qassam, who held the city, repulsed him. Abu Taghlib's ambitions and his contacts with the Fatimids now came to threaten the position of Mufarrij ibn Daghfal ibn al-Jarrah, a Tayy chief and ruler of Ramla.

Abu Taghlib.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Taghlib.question: This was likely done at the behest of Adud al-Dawla, whom _____ had previously recognized as his overlord
Abu Taghlib.fact: Abu Taghlib's ambitions and his contacts with the Fatimids now came to threaten the position of Mufarrij ibn Daghfal ibn al-Jarrah, a Tayy chief and ruler of Ramla. Hoping to sow dissension among the Arab tribes of the area and strengthen Fatimid authority, the Fatimid general Fadl now promised Ramla to Abu Taghlib, who openly allied himself with Mufarrij's rivals, the Banu Uqayl, and attacked Ramla in August 979.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The _____ was Kharijite Berber leader (c. 873–947).
Abu Yazid.fact: Known as the Man on the Donkey (Arabic: صاحب الحمار, romanized: Ṣāhib al-Himār) due to his humble means of transport, Abu Yazid led a rebellion against the Fatimid Caliphate in Ifriqiya (modern Tunisia and eastern Algeria) starting in 944, rallying various Berber tribes and disaffected groups against the Fatimids. Abu Yazid conquered Kairouan for a time, but was eventually driven back and defeated by the Fatimid caliph al-Mansur bi-Nasr Allah in 947, Abu Yazid escaped following a siege, but w...

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Abū Yazīd _____ ibn Kaydād (Arabic: أبو يزيد مخلد بن كيداد;‎ c
Abu Yazid.fact: Abū Yazīd Makhlad ibn Kaydād (Arabic: أبو يزيد مخلد بن كيداد;‎ c.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: 873 – 19 _____ 947), was a member of the Ibadi sect
Abu Yazid.fact: 873 – 19 August 947), was a member of the Ibadi sect.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: He opposed the _____ rule of the Fatimids in North Africa and sought to restore Ibadi dominance in the region
Abu Yazid.fact: He opposed the Ismaili Shia rule of the Fatimids in North Africa and sought to restore Ibadi dominance in the region.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: His forces initially achieved significant victories, even threatening the _____ capital of al-Mahdiyya
Abu Yazid.fact: He opposed the Ismaili Shia rule of the Fatimids in North Africa and sought to restore Ibadi dominance in the region. Known as the Man on the Donkey (Arabic: صاحب الحمار, romanized: Ṣāhib al-Himār) due to his humble means of transport, Abu Yazid led a rebellion against the Fatimid Caliphate in Ifriqiya (modern Tunisia and eastern Algeria) starting in 944, rallying various Berber tribes and disaffected groups against the Fatimids.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Kaydad was a trans-_____ trader, and during his travels took as concubine a Hawwara or Black African slave, Sabika
Abu Yazid.fact: Kaydad was a trans-Saharan trader, and during his travels took as concubine a Hawwara or Black African slave, Sabika.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: 874 south of the Sahara, at _____ or Gao
Abu Yazid.fact: 874 south of the Sahara, at Tadmakka or Gao.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Coupled with his mother's descent, this brought him the sobriquet "the _____" (al-Habashi al-Aswad)
Abu Yazid.fact: Coupled with his mother's descent, this brought him the sobriquet "the Black Ethiop" (al-Habashi al-Aswad).

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The orphaned boy survived through alms, and in his youth became a schoolmaster in the area of Qitun, _____, and Taqyus
Abu Yazid.fact: The orphaned boy survived through alms, and in his youth became a schoolmaster in the area of Qitun, Tozeur, and Taqyus.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: On the way, the _____ overthrew and executed the Rustamid imam, and installed a Fatimid governor in his place
Abu Yazid.fact: Abu Yazid was an eyewitness to the end of the Ibadi imamate in 909: after the overthrow of the Aghlabid emirate by the Isma'ili preacher Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i and his Kutama followers, the latter marched west to Sijilmasa, to bring his hidden master, Abdallah al-Mahdi Billah, back to Ifriqiya to assume the throne of the Fatimid Caliphate. On the way, the Kutama overthrew and executed the Rustamid imam, and installed a Fatimid governor in his place.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: He was arrested in 934 but escaped, and went on the _____ to Mecca
Abu Yazid.fact: He was arrested in 934 but escaped, and went on the Hajj to Mecca.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: In 937 he returned to _____ clandestinely and resumed his preaching
Abu Yazid.fact: In 937 he returned to Tozeur clandestinely and resumed his preaching.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The area had in the previous decades been converted to the Nukkari branch of Ibadi Islam, and was a major centre of the sect, with _____ as its local leader
Abu Yazid.fact: He was denounced and arrested once again, but sprung out of prison by his former teacher Abu Ammar Abd al-Hamid al-A'ma and forty of his armed followers, along with two of Abu Yazid's sons. The area had in the previous decades been converted to the Nukkari branch of Ibadi Islam, and was a major centre of the sect, with Abu Ammar as its local leader.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The Nukkaris rejected the hereditary _____ imams and insisted upon the election of the community's leader
Abu Yazid.fact: The Nukkaris rejected the hereditary Rustamid imams and insisted upon the election of the community's leader.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Thereupon Abu Ammar relinquished his leadership to him as the more worthy one (afḍal), in accordance with the _____ doctrine
Abu Yazid.fact: Thereupon Abu Ammar relinquished his leadership to him as the more worthy one (afḍal), in accordance with the Nukkari doctrine.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Even his pejorative sobriquet al-_____ was often held to have messianic connotations
Abu Yazid.fact: Abu Yazid's movement was the spiritual heir to a number of tendencies endemic in the Maghreb: the Ibadi movement, with its anti-Arab and pro-Berber chauvinism and its insistence that leadership belonged to the "best Muslim", in marked contrast to the Fatimids' claims to a hereditary imamate; the anti-imperial traditions of the great Berber Revolt against the Umayyad Caliphate in 740; and the strong messianic traditions of the Maghreb, which had welcomed and sheltered the Alids persecuted by t...

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The uprising appears to have caught the _____ by surprise
Abu Yazid.fact: The uprising appears to have caught the Fatimids by surprise.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The first major settlement to capitulate was Tébessa, followed by _____, where he was given his famous donkey to ride
Abu Yazid.fact: The first major settlement to capitulate was Tébessa, followed by Marmajanna, where he was given his famous donkey to ride.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: After the surrender of Sbiba, the rebels destroyed a _____ army near Dougga and captured the city
Abu Yazid.fact: Caliph al-Qa'im mobilized his loyal Kutama tribes, but the small and highly mobile bands of Abu Yazid eluded them, and were always able to escape back to the safety of the Aurès. After the surrender of Sbiba, the rebels destroyed a Kutama army near Dougga and captured the city.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: These dispositions left the initiative to the rebels, who attacked _____
Abu Yazid.fact: Al-Qa'im mobilized four armies in response: one to defend the old Aghlabid palace city of Raqqada, one under Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Tamimi to secure the former capital and major city of Ifriqiya, Kairouan, one under the eunuch Bushra to the area of Béja, and the main army under Maysur al-Fata, which was to encamp midway between al-Mahdiya and Kairouan, ready to assist either. These dispositions left the initiative to the rebels, who attacked Bushra.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Béja was sacked for three days, while _____ and his men withdrew, first to Tunis, and then, as its inhabitants wanted to surrender, over sea to Sousse
Abu Yazid.fact: Al-Qa'im mobilized four armies in response: one to defend the old Aghlabid palace city of Raqqada, one under Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Tamimi to secure the former capital and major city of Ifriqiya, Kairouan, one under the eunuch Bushra to the area of Béja, and the main army under Maysur al-Fata, which was to encamp midway between al-Mahdiya and Kairouan, ready to assist either. These dispositions left the initiative to the rebels, who attacked Bushra.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: As a result, the disgruntled and unpaid soldiers of the local militia began deserting to the rebels, until _____ was left with only 400 men
Abu Yazid.fact: Ensconced in Kairouan, Khalil al-Tamimi resisted his officers' calls to march out and confront the rebel army, awaiting the arrival of the main Fatimid army under Maysur al-Fata, but the latter also hesitated to move decisively against the rebels. As a result, the disgruntled and unpaid soldiers of the local militia began deserting to the rebels, until Khalil was left with only 400 men.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Unable to man the city walls with this small a force, he withdrew to the governor's palace next to the _____ of Kairouan
Abu Yazid.fact: Unable to man the city walls with this small a force, he withdrew to the governor's palace next to the Great Mosque of Kairouan.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The rebel leader initially intended to spare Khalil's life, but _____ pointed out that dangerous foes should be killed
Abu Yazid.fact: The rebel leader initially intended to spare Khalil's life, but Abu Ammar pointed out that dangerous foes should be killed.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Shortly after, _____ was sacked as well
Abu Yazid.fact: Shortly after, Sousse was sacked as well.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: He even took two sisters as concubines, disregarding Sunni law, arguing that, as non-_____, they were slaves and he could do as he pleased
Abu Yazid.fact: He even took two sisters as concubines, disregarding Sunni law, arguing that, as non-Kharijites, they were slaves and he could do as he pleased.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The first attack on the city, on _____ January 945, reached the wall of the palace city, but was eventually pushed back
Abu Yazid.fact: The first attack on the city, on 20 January 945, reached the wall of the palace city, but was eventually pushed back.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The city was placed under blockade, which lasted until 16 _____ 945
Abu Yazid.fact: The city was placed under blockade, which lasted until 16 September 945.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Most of his men were untrained peasants, who now returned to their fields, or out for plunder; the _____ leader could count firmly only on the Hawwara
Abu Yazid.fact: Most of his men were untrained peasants, who now returned to their fields, or out for plunder; the Kharijite leader could count firmly only on the Hawwara.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: As a result, the siege was not very effective, and _____ sallies sometimes found the enemy camp empty
Abu Yazid.fact: The Fatimid position was difficult, as the ships bringing in grain supplies ran aground and were captured by the rebels, but Abu Yazid also faced problems. As a result, the siege was not very effective, and Fatimid sallies sometimes found the enemy camp empty.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: However, the inhabitants of _____ had by now turned against him
Abu Yazid.fact: The rebel army suffered heavy losses, and Abu Yazid was forced to retreat to Kairouan. However, the inhabitants of Kairouan had by now turned against him.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Tunis, Béja and al-_____ followed suit
Abu Yazid.fact: Tunis, Béja and al-Aribus followed suit. A similar fate befell Béja and al-Aribus.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: A similar fate befell Béja and al-_____
Abu Yazid.fact: Tunis, Béja and al-Aribus followed suit. A similar fate befell Béja and al-Aribus.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Its commander, the veteran _____ partisan Ali ibn Hamdun al-Andalusi, was mortally wounded and died shortly after
Abu Yazid.fact: During the following months, heavy fighting between Abu Yazid's and the Fatimid forces occurred at Tunis, which was captured and recaptured by both sides, and left almost completely destroyed. Abu Yazid's son Ayyub defeated a Fatimid army from Msila.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: In November, Ayyub was defeated by _____ troops under al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kalbi, before in turn defeating the latter
Abu Yazid.fact: Abu Yazid's son Ayyub defeated a Fatimid army from Msila. Its commander, the veteran Fatimid partisan Ali ibn Hamdun al-Andalusi, was mortally wounded and died shortly after.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: As the year was late and the sailing season over, however, the _____ fleet was set to sail in the next year
Abu Yazid.fact: Seeking allies against the Fatimids, Abu Yazid sent some Kairouan notables as envoys to the Spanish Umayyads. After this first embassy was well received, Abu Yazid sent Ayyub to pledge allegiance to the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Rahman III, who in turn promised to send support.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: On 17 May 946, _____ al-Qa'im died and was succeeded by his son Isma'il al-Mansur Billah
Abu Yazid.fact: On 17 May 946, Caliph al-Qa'im died and was succeeded by his son Isma'il al-Mansur Billah.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: All public business and ceremonies were still conducted in al-Qa'im's name, and al-_____ acted ostensibly only as his heir-designate
Abu Yazid.fact: On 17 May 946, Caliph al-Qa'im died and was succeeded by his son Isma'il al-Mansur Billah. To avoid giving the rebels any advantage, al-Mansur and his government hid the death of his father, a task made easier by the reclusive life al-Qa'im had led, rarely venturing out of his palace during his reign.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Even the regnal name of al-_____ ("the Victorious") was only publicly assumed after the final suppression of the uprising
Abu Yazid.fact: On 17 May 946, Caliph al-Qa'im died and was succeeded by his son Isma'il al-Mansur Billah. To avoid giving the rebels any advantage, al-Mansur and his government hid the death of his father, a task made easier by the reclusive life al-Qa'im had led, rarely venturing out of his palace during his reign.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: After ransoming _____ from captivity, he established a camp two days' march from the city
Abu Yazid.fact: After ransoming Abu Ammar from captivity, he set up a camp two days' march from the city.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The two armies remained entrenched around _____ for the next two months, engaging in frequent clashes
Abu Yazid.fact: In the meantime, al-Mansur issued a full amnesty to the notables of Kairouan in return for their renewed loyalty, and on 28 May, the caliph entered the city with his troops, and set up a fortified camp south of it. The two armies remained entrenched around Kairouan for the next two months, engaging in frequent clashes.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: More and more followers abandoned his camp, and only the Hawwara and _____ remained steadfastly loyal to him
Abu Yazid.fact: More and more followers abandoned his camp, and only the Hawwara and Banu Kamlan Berbers remained steadfastly loyal to him.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: In the meantime, al-Hasan al-Kalbi gathered the Kutama levies at _____, and recaptured Béja and Tunis
Abu Yazid.fact: In the meantime, al-Hasan al-Kalbi gathered the Kutama levies at Constantine, and recaptured Béja and Tunis.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: By early _____, the Fatimid caliph recovered Marmajanna, Béja, Billizma, Tubna (ancient Tubunae), and Biskra
Abu Yazid.fact: By early December, the Fatimid caliph recovered Marmajanna, Béja, Billizma, Tubna (ancient Tubunae), and Biskra.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Al-_____ tried to follow him, but at Biskra he was forced to stop, as the local guides warned him that the route followed by the Kharijite leader and his followers was extremely dangerous
Abu Yazid.fact: Al-Mansur tried to follow him, but at Biskra he was forced to stop, as the local guides warned him that the route followed by the Kharijite leader and his followers was extremely dangerous.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: As a result, the _____ army turned back from Biskra to Tubna, and thence marched west, along the northern shore of Chott el Hodna
Abu Yazid.fact: As a result, the Fatimid army turned back from Biskra to Tubna, and thence marched west, along the northern shore of Chott el Hodna.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The victory allowed al-_____ to secure his control over Msila, and brought the submission of the local tribes and towns
Abu Yazid.fact: The victory allowed al-Mansur to secure his control over Msila, and brought the submission of the local tribes and towns. Shortly after, Abu Yazid launched an attack on al-Mansur's army camp near Msila, but was again beaten back.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: When the _____ troops pursued him there in late December, he again fled to the desert, and this time al-Mansur was determined to follow him
Abu Yazid.fact: When the Fatimid troops pursued him there in late December, he again fled to the desert, and this time al-Mansur was determined to follow him. After a grueling eleven-day march in the desert he was forced to turn back, only for the heavy winter to take further toll on his army; the Fatimid caliph himself fell heavily ill due to the rigours of the campaign and was bedridden for two weeks.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: On 30 _____ 947, the Fatimid army returned to Msila to rest and await spring
Abu Yazid.fact: On 30 January 947, the Fatimid army returned to Msila to rest and await spring.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: It was only the protestations of his followers from the Hawwara and _____ tribes that convinced him to persist
Abu Yazid.fact: It was only the protestations of his followers from the Hawwara and Banu Kamlan tribes that convinced him to persist.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: On 6 March, al-_____, accompanied by 4,000 of his own cavalry and 500 Sanhaja, set out for Azbih
Abu Yazid.fact: On 6 March, al-Mansur, accompanied by 4,000 of his own cavalry and 500 Sanhaja, set out for Azbih. His son Yunus was killed, and 1070 severed heads of his followers were sent as token of victory to Kairouan by al-Mansur.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: His son Yunus was killed, and _____ severed heads of his followers were sent as token of victory to Kairouan by al-Mansur
Abu Yazid.fact: His son Yunus was killed, and 1070 severed heads of his followers were sent as token of victory to Kairouan by al-Mansur.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Al-_____ did not immediately attack him there, but instead methodically subdued the surrounding mountains to deprive him of any support
Abu Yazid.fact: His son Yunus was killed, and 1070 severed heads of his followers were sent as token of victory to Kairouan by al-Mansur. Al-Mansur did not immediately attack him there, but instead methodically subdued the surrounding mountains to deprive him of any support.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: On 26 April, al-_____ began his siege of the fortress, with siege engines shipped from Ifriqiya over sea and carried over the mountains
Abu Yazid.fact: Al-Mansur did not immediately attack him there, but instead methodically subdued the surrounding mountains to deprive him of any support. On 26 April, al-Mansur began his siege of the fortress, with siege engines shipped from Ifriqiya over sea and carried over the mountains.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: In early June, the neighbouring fortresses of _____ and Aqqar, also held by rebels, surrendered, and on 14 August 947, the final attack on Kiyana was launched
Abu Yazid.fact: In early June, the neighbouring fortresses of Shakir and Aqqar, also held by rebels, surrendered, and on 14 August 947, the final attack on Kiyana was launched.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: Heavily wounded, he was interrogated by the caliph, before dying of his injuries after four days, on 19 _____
Abu Yazid.fact: Heavily wounded, he was interrogated by the caliph, before dying of his injuries after four days, on 19 August.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: His severed head was dispatched to the caliph, who sent it together with the stuffed skin of his father to _____ as a warning
Abu Yazid.fact: His severed head was dispatched to the caliph, who sent it together with the stuffed skin of his father to Sicily as a warning.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The various _____ legends in Hausa folklore describe how Bayajida, son of the king of Baghdad, came to Bornu and married the ruler's daughter
Abu Yazid.fact: The various Bayajida legends in Hausa folklore describe how Bayajida, son of the king of Baghdad, came to Bornu and married the ruler's daughter. and Bayajida may be identical with the Ibāḍite sectary Abū Yazīd who resisted the Fāṭimids of Tunisia until he was killed by them in 947.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: and _____ may be identical with the Ibāḍite sectary Abū Yazīd who resisted the Fāṭimids of Tunisia until he was killed by them in 947
Abu Yazid.fact: The various Bayajida legends in Hausa folklore describe how Bayajida, son of the king of Baghdad, came to Bornu and married the ruler's daughter. and Bayajida may be identical with the Ibāḍite sectary Abū Yazīd who resisted the Fāṭimids of Tunisia until he was killed by them in 947.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: He later fled and came to _____, fathering the founders of the seven Hausa states
Abu Yazid.fact: He later fled and came to Daura, fathering the founders of the seven Hausa states.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The debris of his army may have fled across the Sahara and arrived in Bornu, then north of _____
Abu Yazid.fact: The debris of his army may have fled across the Sahara and arrived in Bornu, then north of Lake Chad.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: After some time a part of this rabble which had remained unassimilated moved south-west and interbred with the indigenous inhabitants round _____, forming the Hausa aristocracies
Abu Yazid.fact: After some time a part of this rabble which had remained unassimilated moved south-west and interbred with the indigenous inhabitants round Daura, forming the Hausa aristocracies.

Abu Yazid.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yazid.question: The first attack on the city, on 20 _____ 945, reached the wall of the palace city, but was eventually pushed back
Abu Yazid.fact: Abu Yazid arrived before the Fatimid capital on 9 January 945. The first attack on the city, on 20 January 945, reached the wall of the palace city, but was eventually pushed back.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: The _____ was Marinid Sultan (r. 1258–1286).
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.answer: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: 1212 – 20 March 1286) was a Marinid ruler. He was the fourth son of Marinid founder Abd al-Haqq, and succeeded his brother Abu Yahya in 1258.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: He was the fourth son of Marinid founder Abd al-Haqq, and succeeded his brother Abu Yahya in 1258. At the time of Abu Yahya's death in July, 1258, the Marinids were installed in Fez and controlled eastern and northern Morocco, the Almohads reduced to the southerly districts around their capital, Marrakesh.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: He was the son of Abd al-Haqq I and Oum el-Iman bint Ali el-_____, a Zenata woman
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: He was the son of Abd al-Haqq I and Oum el-Iman bint Ali el-Bethary, a Zenata woman.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: Some sources add her mother to be known as Oum el Youm and a daughter of a Zenata clan leader of the _____ region
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Some sources add her mother to be called Oum el Youm and a daughter of a Zenata clan leader of the Tafersit region.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: In September, _____, in a surprise attack, a Christian naval force from Spain, probably Castilian, landed on the Atlantic coast of Morocco and seized the city of Salé
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: In September, 1260, in a surprise attack, a Christian naval force from Spain, probably Castilian, landed on the Atlantic coast of Morocco and seized the city of Salé.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: It was the first known direct encounter between the _____ and the Christian powers of the Iberian Peninsula
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Although Abu Yahya had designated his son as successor in Fez, Abu Yusuf Yaqub, then a governor in Taza, managed, with only a little difficulty, to displace his nephew and get himself acknowledged as emir of the Marinids. It was the first known direct encounter between the Marinids and the Christian powers of the Iberian Peninsula.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: Abu Yusuf decided against a retaliatory raid, and instead focused on reducing the _____ resistance in the south
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Abu Yusuf decided against a retaliatory raid, and instead focused on reducing the Almohad resistance in the south. Changing tactics, he decided to sponsor the rebellious Almohad chieftain Abu Dabbus in his struggle against his cousin, the Almohad caliph Abu Hafs Umar al-Murtada.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: The Abdalwadid ruler Yaghmorassan of Tlemcen was happy enough to align with the Granadan-Aragonese, and was promptly punished by a new Marinid campaign against Tlemcen in _____
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Abu Yusuf decided against a retaliatory raid, and instead focused on reducing the Almohad resistance in the south. Changing tactics, he decided to sponsor the rebellious Almohad chieftain Abu Dabbus in his struggle against his cousin, the Almohad caliph Abu Hafs Umar al-Murtada.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Changing tactics, he decided to sponsor the rebellious Almohad chieftain Abu Dabbus in his struggle against his cousin, the Almohad caliph Abu Hafs Umar al-Murtada. But once Abu Dabbus seized Marrakesh in 1266, he broke his treaty with the Marinids and refused to pass Marrakesh over to them.

But once Abu Dabbus seized Marrakesh in 1266, he broke his treaty with the Marinids and refused to pass Marrakesh over to them.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: But once Abu Dabbus seized Marrakesh in _____, he broke his treaty with the Marinids and refused to pass Marrakesh over to them
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: But once Abu Dabbus seized Marrakesh in 1266, he broke his treaty with the Marinids and refused to pass Marrakesh over to them.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: Abu Yusuf broke off his campaign against the errant Almohad client to deal with the Tlemcen intervention, defeating the Abdalwadids at a battle by the Moulouya in _____
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Abu Yusuf broke off his campaign against the errant Almohad client to deal with the Tlemcen intervention, defeating the Abdalwadids at a battle by the Moulouya in 1268.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: Abu Yusuf promptly returned to the south, defeated the forces of Abu Dabbus and entered Marrakesh on 8 September _____, putting a final end to the Almohad Caliphate
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Abu Yusuf promptly returned to the south, defeated the forces of Abu Dabbus and entered Marrakesh on 8 September 1269, putting a final end to the Almohad Caliphate.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: The Marinids were masters of _____, and Abu Yusuf Yaqub took up the title of 'Prince of the Muslims' (amir el-moslimin), the old title used by the Almoravid rulers in the 11th-12th centuries
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: The Marinids were masters of Morocco, and Abu Yusuf Yaqub took up the title of 'Prince of the Muslims' (amir el-moslimin), the old title used by the Almoravid rulers in the 11th-12th centuries.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.question: Like the _____, the Marinids never adopted the caliphal title (amir al-mu'minin), believing it to be an impious pretension (although the contemporary Hafsid rulers of Ifriqiya would soon take it up)
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.fact: Like the Almoravids, the Marinids never adopted the caliphal title (amir al-mu'minin), believing it to be an impious pretension (although the contemporary Hafsid rulers of Ifriqiya would soon take it up). The Marinids resisted the temptation of relocating their capital to the Marrakesh, citadel of the Almoravids and Almohads, preferring to base themselves at Fez.

Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subject: Indian Languages
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq.subSubject: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq

Abu-Mansuri Shahnameh.subject: Indian Languages
Abu-Mansuri Shahnameh.question: The _____ was Persian literary book.
Abu-Mansuri Shahnameh.fact: The Abu-Mansuri Shahnameh or Shahnameh of Abu-Mansur (Persian: شاهنامهٔ ابومنصوری) was a prose epic and history of the Persian Empire before Muslim conquests, composed at the order of Abu Mansur Muhammad in 346 AH (April 957 AD). The Abu-Mansuri Shahnameh is now lost, but its preface, which consists of 15 pages, has survived and is one of the oldest examples of Persian prose and is considered one of the most valuable heritages of Persian literature.
